RE-CONFIRMATION vs current main (panel condition #1) — DECISIVE:
- origin/main has 0 refs to _branch_is_staged_promotion (the 3ebb staged-force-push fix); dd123-6 has 7. BOTH have cca8 (_sync_branch_against_default + _publish_rebased_branch + 'gh pr merge --auto --rebase'). So the friction was NOT from running pre-cca8 logic — the architecture lens's 'self-inflicted' hypothesis is REFUTED.
- On PR2 (staged->main), origin/main runs _publish_rebased_branch $BRANCH (force-push the rebased STAGED ref) with NO staged-* guard => bug e1bf GH013 rejection, CONFIRMED REACHABLE on current main. The 3ebb staged-skip avoids GH013 but leaves the staged ref stale => determinate conflict (what this session hit; re-stageable).
- CONCLUSIONS: (1) the 3ebb pin was correct/necessary (main would hard-fail GH013); the staged-force-push fix is an improvement, not a regression. (2) e1bf is LIVE on main now, affecting every staged promotion; its fix is the _branch_is_staged_promotion guard carried in PR #684 (landing) — so landing #684 fixes e1bf on main. (3) The structural F2 tension (protected-staged-ref cannot be both un-force-pushed AND kept current) is genuinely unsolved; O3/linear-history makes PR2 a clean rebase-merge but does not by itself remove staged-staleness-on-advance. Panel's 'O3 gated on e1bf' refines to: e1bf fix is in-flight (#684); prioritize landing it.
